editorialLexicalPolicy.evidenceBoundary: Spanish realization options and constraints only. These entries never override source surface, morphology, syntax, discourse, or canonical corpus evidence.
editorialLexicalPolicy.instruction: Choose the Spanish realization of nephesh from its construction and participants. Alma remains permitted but is never automatic; do not import immortality, separability, or a body-soul contrast that the source does not express.

spanishOptions.when: The construction identifies a whole living human or animal, especially with the living-creature expression.
Human beings are counted, identified as members of a group, or referred to as whole persons.
Life is killed, preserved, endangered, sought, surrendered, or recovered.
The construction concerns the inner person, personal identity, desire, or a contrast that this established Spanish term preserves accurately.
The syntax and discourse specifically require one of these contextual relations and natural Spanish supports it.

avoid: using alma as an automatic gloss
using vida or persona as an automatic replacement
adding immortality or separability without source evidence
merging nephesh with neshamah or ruach

editorialLexicalPolicyReview.title: Alma, vida y persona
editorialLexicalPolicyReview.summary: Canonical usage includes animals, whole living beings, counted persons, endangered life, desire, and inner identity; no single Spanish realization covers every occurrence.
